note: Qwen3.5 is natively image-text-to-text; this recipe is the vision tower (patch16, 2x2 merge, interleaved 3-D mrope) + chunked-prefill graph, paired with each sibling recipe's text decoder unchanged. Vision tower depth/width differs by decoder size (0.8B/2B share a 12-block tower; 4B's is 24 blocks — see qwen3.5-4b recipe). NOT an official OE-LLM Omni-style package: Qwen3.5's tower geometry (patch16, mean/std 0.5, mrope_section [11,11,10] interleaved) is different from Omni's (patch14, CLIP constants, mrope_section [16,24,24] contiguous) and must not be copied across.

quantisation.vision_activations: int16, per-linear calibrated on 48 COCO val2017 images
quantisation.note: Massive-activation channels in the tower's deep MLP blocks (not RMSNorm/variance) clip under a flat calibration range. Recalibrate per bucket AND per decoder size independently — see README. Gate acceptance on real photos only; a synthetic reference image reads a misleadingly low cosine relative to the real-photo case.

rejected_builds.name: Omni vision settings copied onto a Qwen3.5 tower
rejected_builds.why: patch14 vs Qwen3.5's patch16, CLIP mean/std vs Qwen3.5's flat 0.5/0.5, mrope_section [16,24,24] contiguous vs Qwen3.5's [11,11,10] interleaved. All four compile and load without error; a mismatch produces shape-correct garbage discovered only once an image is fed, not at compile or text-smoke-test time.

rejected_builds.name: 336px bucket
rejected_builds.why: patch16 x merge2 requires side % 32 == 0; 336/16=21 is odd, no clean 2x2 merge. Reject before compile, not after.

rejected_builds.name: flat/synthetic vision-tower calibration
rejected_builds.why: A flat calibration range across all tower blocks clips the deep-MLP massive-activation channels (2-4x larger than earlier blocks). A synthetic/rendered reference image under-represents the real-photo activation distribution, so a build can measure a misleadingly low cosine on a synthetic gate image (~0.987) while actually being fine on real photos (~0.997) -- OR the reverse could happen with a different synthetic image, which is exactly why synthetic gating is rejected as a methodology, not just this one instance of it.

rejected_builds.name: S600 (nash-p) 4B prefill graph at default hbcompile optimisation
rejected_builds.why: Native compiler crash (not a catchable exception): 'error: B30 VPU ops do not support circular buffer'. Specific to {nash-p backend, this graph shape at 4B scale, default opt level} -- the identical graph compiles fine for nash-p at 2B scale, and for 4B on nash-m (S100P) at the default level. --probe (export+convert only) passes clean both before and after the fix, confirming the graph structure itself was never the problem. Fixed by compiling at hbcompile opt=0 (~46 min, same correctness as the working nash-m build).

s100p.flow: docker stop the resident serving container; bllm.load(dir) in isolation; chat() with a test image, contrast against the same question without the image; restore the stopped container

s600.flow: hrt_model_exec model_info on the compiled vision tower and prefill graph directly for load-only verification; full bllm.load() + chat(images=[...]) attempted for 2b once the hobot-dnn-s600 dependency and a NativeVlm multi-core crash were both fixed
s600.note: 2b end-to-end chat() runs (crash fixed) but is intermittently wrong (~40-50% empty output, root cause unknown) -- NOT counted as verified. 4b end-to-end not attempted at all. See qwen3.5-vlm README S600 section.
